motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Transportation Master Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Transportation Master Plan. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Transportation Master Plan put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed adopting the Transportation Master Plan, the city's long-range plan for its road network.
motions.impact: No road decisions are locked in by this. The plan shapes where future roads and improvements go, and it has to come back to the council before it takes effect.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to deny an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Parking rule changes rejected
motions.summary: The council moved to reject proposed changes to the city's parking rules.
motions.impact: The parking rules stay exactly as they are today. There is nothing new you need to do, and no new restrictions on where you park.

motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the bundle of items passed together in one vote; the record does not list what was in it.
motions.impact: Nothing in the record points to a specific change for residents, because the items grouped into this single vote were not listed.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 0.156 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #49:601:0080) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal. Cou ncilmember Gray seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 0.156 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #49:601:0080) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal. Cou ncilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sale of small city parcel delayed
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on selling a 0.156-acre piece of city property, and on the terms of that sale.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — the city holds onto the parcel until the council revisits the sale.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of up to 20.35 acres of Public Real Property known as the Bypass Road
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of up to 20.35 acres of Public Real Property known as the Bypass Road. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Bypass Road land sale put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on selling up to 20.35 acres of city-owned land known as the Bypass Road.
motions.impact: The city keeps the 20.35 acres for now. Any sale would have to come back to the council before it could go through.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sign rule changes put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's sign rules, which cover what signs are allowed and how sign permits work.
motions.impact: Nothing changes yet — the sign and permit rules on the books today still apply until the council takes the item back up.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah approving a Franchise Agreement with Zayo Group, LLC
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah approving a Franchise Agreement with Zayo Group, LLC. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Zayo fiber franchise agreement put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on a franchise agreement with Zayo Group, LLC, holding the item over rather than voting it up or down.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents right now. The agreement is on hold and would have to come back to the council before it could take effect.
